clue.text: Copy company used in recording feature of Mass

indicators.note: something used in a thing is put inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: a compact disc is a recording
to ape is to copy
standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm that photocopies sheet music is hired to record part of a church Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass is not the church service but the abbreviation for Massachusetts, whose coastline has the famous hooked peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked peninsula is a geographical landmark of the US state of Massachusetts, abbreviated Mass.

clue.text: Get to grips with illegal parking restriction

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grip or fasten tightly
second meaning: the wheel lock fitted to a badly parked car

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to tackle the problem of illegal parking.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hold firmly; as a noun it is the immobilising device fixed to an offending vehicle's wheel.

clue.text: Choose to finish early — unexpectedly cool bit of wind

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping short, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to pick is to choose

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly comes out in an unforeseen order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone decides to leave early, and a cool breeze blows unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of wind' is not a breeze but one member of an orchestra's wind section.
explanation.definitionFit: The small high-pitched flute is one instrument in the woodwind section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Rabbit on in company, vacuously

indicators.note: one word sits in another, placed between its letters
emptied of its contents, the word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: the word company emptied of its middle
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone chatters on emptily at a business, rabbit being slang for talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' reads as British slang for talking endlessly, but Rabbit alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a rabbit, or its fur, found in heraldry and the Bible.

clue.text: Had reservations about using this route

definitions.text: Had reservations about using this route

parts.note: surface reading: had doubts about taking a particular road
setter's reading: the road has central reservations, strips dividing its two sides

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a central reservation is the strip separating opposite lanes on a big road, so this road literally has reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: A British road with two separate carriageways split by a central reservation strip.

clue.text: Misbehaving is close to the bone

indicators.note: letters that misbehave refuse to stay in their proper places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour that is close to the bone, near the mark of decency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to the bone' is an idiom for near-offensive, which hides that bone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the term for a very small bone, such as those in the middle ear.

clue.text: Correctly ascertaining one's railway connections?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for heading towards the correct conclusion
second meaning, taken literally: a train on the proper line of rails

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for making progress towards the truth is taken literally as a train on the proper rails.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means pursuing a line of thought that will lead to success, borrowed from trains.

clue.text: Arrange release from prison sentence when winter finishes

parts.note: to spring a prisoner is to free them
doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: Someone plans to get a convict freed once winter is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The season after winter is the period of spring, so it begins when winter ends.

clue.text: Some Spaniards are at a family gathering

definitions.note: plural, the answer as a noun is singular, but it is also the people collectively

indicators.note: a group gathering something up collects it within itself

parts.note: a clan is a family group
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some people from Spain are attending a family get-together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family gathering' reads as a reunion; gathering is the device that puts two words inside the family.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalonia is a region of Spain, and its people are one group of Spaniards.

clue.text: It's a bit creepy to celebrate jumped-up local inhabitants

definitions.note: plural phrase for a population type adapted locally

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
a bit of the following words means a run of their letters is taken

parts.note: letters spanning these words

explanation.surface: It seems creepy for local people to throw a party for a social upstart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumped-up' looks like a sneer at the inhabitants, but in a down clue it turns the letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology this is a population of a species adapted genetically to its particular local environment.

clue.text: When small change keeps standard reached in judo rising?

parts.note: as can mean when

indicators.note: something that keeps another holds it inside

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
a dan is a grade in judo and other martial arts

explanation.surface: A puzzle about coins and judo grades, asking whether someone is rising in the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the judo picture; rising is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the ascendant is climbing or gaining power, so the adjective sense matches rising.

clue.text: Irrational number in sequence — pi?

indicators.note: a number of letters in sequence means a consecutive run taken from within the word

parts.note: consecutive letters inside this word

explanation.surface: A maths question: is pi an irrational number in a sequence?
explanation.walkthrough: Pi famously is irrational, yet it is also defined as circumference over diameter, which is the answer's kind of thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pi is the quotient of a circle's circumference and diameter, an example of this relation between two quantities.

clue.text: Support offered 14's neighbour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something that holds up
second meaning: the rugby forward packing beside the player at 14-across

explanation.walkthrough: In a rugby scrum the hooker is flanked on each side by a prop forward.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a physical support and the front-row rugby position either side of the hooker.

clue.text: Vet taking gamble on film script

parts.note: to vet candidates is to screen them
to play is to gamble

explanation.surface: An animal doctor bets money on a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Vet is not the animal doctor but the verb meaning to check.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the written text of a movie, with dialogue and directions for the actors.

clue.text: Quickly dismiss satirical item, badly let down, perhaps?

parts.note: a skit is a short satirical sketch

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
down is an example of out, as in out of action or not working

explanation.surface: A comedy sketch that has disappointed is swiftly written off.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket term: a bowling side skittles out batsmen by taking wickets in quick succession.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the phrase means to bowl out a batting side cheaply and rapidly.

clue.text: Rugby player — a pro?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the front-row forward who hooks the ball in a scrum

explanation.walkthrough: Pro looks like a professional sportsman; it is short for prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a scrum position in rugby and, informally, a sex worker.

clue.text: Seriously concerned with how decimals work, close to innumerate

parts.note: the decimal system counts in units of ten

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter is wanted

parts.note: the end of this word

explanation.surface: Someone bad at maths is earnestly worried about decimals.
explanation.definitionFit: An intense person is earnest and deeply absorbed, which matches being seriously concerned.

clue.text: Car designer has problem computing storage space, mostly

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a bug is a fault in software
the roof space used for storage

explanation.surface: An automotive engineer is struggling with computer storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storage space' sounds like computer memory but is the room under the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Ettore Bugatti was the Italian-French engineer who founded the luxury sports car marque.

clue.text: Bill endangered this species? Expert takes a look

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert
taken as written
lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A specialist investigates whether a hunter threatened an animal species.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffalo Bill Cody earned his nickname by slaughtering thousands of American bison.
explanation.definitionFit: The American bison is popularly called by this name, and the frontiersman nearly wiped it out.

clue.text: Tynesider, say, must turn up or fail at some stage

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
taken as written
everything fails and dies eventually

explanation.surface: A man from Newcastle must show up or fail at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it marks Tynesider as an example; it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nickname for a native of Tyneside, the area around Newcastle in north-east England.

clue.text: Hooked by meat, tucked in

parts.note: ham is a meat
to tuck in is to eat heartily

explanation.surface: Someone was lured by meat and then tucked into it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooked reads as tempted; it is the anatomical adjective meaning hook-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the adjective means having a hook-like process, as in the wrist bone so named.

clue.text: Warning about interest rate that helps plant survive

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it

parts.note: a toot of a horn is a warning
annual percentage rate

explanation.surface: A caution about the interest rate that keeps a factory going.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a factory; it is a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The main downward root of a plant anchors it and draws water from deep soil.

clue.text: Sketches of Cambridge

parts.note: surface reading: drawings of the university town
setter's reading: the student comedy troupe there, famous for revue sketches

explanation.walkthrough: The Cambridge University dramatic club of this name launched many British comedians through its sketch revues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambridge University theatrical club performs comedy revues and is named after stage-front lamps.

clue.text: One part of the opera

parts.note: surface reading: an aria or act in a stage work
setter's reading: opera is the Latin plural of this word, so one of them is the singular

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for a work has opera as its plural, so one of the opera is a single work.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a single musical composition, and its plural form in Latin is opera.

clue.text: Twitcher's almost last in hide to see birds flying

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

indicators.note: almost the last means the letter just before the final one

parts.note: the second-to-last letter of this word

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher waits in a hide to see birds in flight.
explanation.walkthrough: A twitcher is a keen birdwatcher, and a hide is a screened shelter for watching birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of wild geese or swans in flight is called by this collective noun.

clue.text: Put up with undisguised chatting

indicators.note: chatting is speech, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: undisguised means plain or exposed

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates frank, open conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate or endure something is to put up with it.

clue.text: Sound version of material taped

definitions.meaning: first meaning: relating to sound, as an adjective
second meaning: a recording made for listening

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a reliable copy of a recording; split, each half defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the adjective for anything heard, and the noun for recorded listening matter such as tapes.

clue.text: How baleen is processed?

indicators.note: material that is processed is broken down and reworked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about how the filtering plates in a whale's mouth are treated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: baleen, once processed, is sold under this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen, the horny plates whales use to filter food, was traded as a flexible material for corsets.

clue.text: Too much time consumed with obvious intentions

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside another

parts.note: overly means excessively
standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone who has spent too long eating has made their aims plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly and undisguised means acting with plain, visible purpose.

clue.text: English deserter harboured by family getting a bit horny?

indicators.note: something harboured is sheltered within something else

parts.note: kin are relatives
standard abbreviation for English
a rat deserts a sinking ship

explanation.surface: An English runaway sheltered by relatives starts feeling amorous.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny is not lustful but made of horn: this protein is what horn consists of.
explanation.definitionFit: The fibrous protein forms horns, hair and nails, so it is the substance of anything horny.
